scenes.narration: Cold water does not start with adaptation. It starts with a gasp reflex you cannot consciously override.
That gasp can pull water into your lungs, which is why open water is dangerous even for strong swimmers.
Within seconds your blood vessels clamp shut and blood pressure jumps sharply, which is why cold exposure is risky for untrained hearts.
Temperature decides severity. Water near fifteen degrees produces a far stronger shock response than water near twenty five.
Past the first minute, adrenaline and noradrenaline surge, and that is the alertness people report afterwards. Most studies on it remain small.
Start with cold water at the end of a normal shower. The controlled dose is where any benefit lives.
